fact: The Vasa sank in 1628 on its maiden voyage in Stockholm harbor
The gun ports sat barely a meter above the waterline
source: Vasa Museum — the lower gun ports were approximately 1 meter above the waterline

fact: A gust of wind caused the ship to heel and water flooded through the open gun ports
source: Vasa Museum and contemporary accounts from the 1628 inquiry
Vasa Museum — the ship carried 64 guns (48 × 24-pounders and others)

fact: Thirty people drowned in the sinking
source: Estimates range from 30 to 50 deaths; 30 is the commonly cited lower figure from the Vasa Museum

fact: The ship sank in sight of a crowd that had gathered to watch its departure
source: Contemporary accounts referenced in 'Vasa I: The Archaeology of a Swedish Warship of 1628' by Fred Hocker (2011)
